headline: Computational methods recover per-cell and domain biology from spatial transcriptomics
label: Computational Spatial Transcriptomics Methods
summary: Recent work pairs histology-based single-cell prediction, 3D reconstruction, and platform benchmarking with spatial inference methods.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference that couples tissue imaging, spatial graph structure, and expression to recover per-cell or per-domain biology from spot-level or aggregated spatial data. sCellST predicts single-cell expression from H&E images, and stACN jointly denoises spatial expression while identifying spatial domains. Spa3D reconstructs 3D structure from 2D slices with a graph convolutional network, and CIPHER optimizes encoding matrices and cell embeddings for aggregated experiments. Deconvolution benchmarks evaluate reference choice for Cell2location and RCTD in breast cancer, and marker-based scoring rivals complex models for rare cell types. SegJointGene links segmentation with spatial gene prioritization. The new elements are histology-derived single-cell prediction and systematic cross-platform benchmarking on matched FFPE tumor sections, but the set is heterogeneous, spanning proteomics, epigenomics, and bulk clonal inference.
